syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Exploring Society India and Beyond Part-II

topics.title: India's Agricultural Landscape
topics.ncert_sections: India's Agricultural Landscape

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what the term agriculture covers, including its allied activities.
State the importance of agriculture to India's output, workforce and women workers.

topics.title: Echoes from the Past
topics.ncert_sections: Echoes from the Past

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the archaeological evidence for early farming and intercropping in the Indian subcontinent.
Identify ancient Indian texts that record knowledge of agriculture, seeds and grafting.

topics.title: Climate, Seasons, and Crops
topics.ncert_sections: Climate, Seasons, and Crops; The monsoon and agriculture; The rhythm of seasons and crops

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how India's climatic diversity and agroclimatic zones guide what crops are grown.
Explain the role of the southwest and northeast monsoons in Indian farming.
Classify crops into the kharif, rabi and zaid cropping seasons.

topics.title: Soil, the Foundation of Cultivation
topics.ncert_sections: Soil, the Foundation of Cultivation; Soils of India; Soil-crop linkages

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how soil and humus are formed from rock and organic matter.
Distinguish the major soil types of India by their formation, properties and crops.

topics.title: Nurturing the Soil
topics.ncert_sections: Nurturing the soil

concepts.learning_objective: Explain traditional soil-care methods such as crop rotation, multiple cropping and contour ploughing.
Explain contemporary soil-conservation methods such as terracing and afforestation.

topics.title: Water and Seeds
topics.ncert_sections: Water: Rain-Fed vs. Irrigated Agriculture; Seeds

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish rain-fed agriculture from irrigated agriculture and their challenges.
Compare traditional irrigation systems with modern drip and sprinkler irrigation.
Explain traditional and modern seed practices and the issue of dependence on seed companies.

topics.title: Agricultural Practices: Traditional Wisdom and Modern Innovations
topics.ncert_sections: Traditional farming systems; Contemporary agriculture; Sustainable pathways

concepts.learning_objective: Describe traditional farming systems such as terrace farming, kulagar and gokrishi.
Evaluate the gains and the limits of the Green Revolution.
Explain how sustainable agriculture combines modern productivity with traditional practices.

topics.title: The Role of the Government and Challenges
topics.ncert_sections: The Role of the Government; Challenges

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the government supports farmers with inputs, insurance and markets.
Analyse challenges such as small landholdings, climate change and stress on river basins.

topics.title: Framing the neighbourhood: land and maritime neighbours
topics.ncert_sections: Framing the Neighbourhood

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish India's land-border neighbours from her maritime neighbours with examples.
Explain how India's coastline and peninsular shape give her a central place in the Indian Ocean.
Describe regionalism as working together with neighbours for peace, stability and shared progress.

topics.title: India's largest neighbour China, and Pakistan
topics.ncert_sections: India and her largest neighbour; India and Pakistan

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the geographical, cultural and trade links between India and China.
Describe the India-Pakistan border and the mix of conflict and shared heritage between the two.
Explain the purpose and significance of the Kartarpur Corridor.

topics.title: Bangladesh and Nepal
topics.ncert_sections: A newborn neighbour; In the lap of the Himalayas

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how history, culture, language and rivers link India and Bangladesh.
Explain why the jointly managed Sundarban mangroves matter for biodiversity and climate resilience.
Explain the India-Nepal open border and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship.

topics.title: Bhutan and the schools of Buddhism
topics.ncert_sections: The 'Land of the Thunder Dragon'

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the economic and spiritual ties between India and Bhutan.
Explain how Bhutan's Gross National Happiness Index differs from GDP as a measure of progress.
Identify the Theravada, Mahayana and Vajrayana schools of Buddhism and where they spread.

topics.title: Myanmar and Afghanistan
topics.ncert_sections: India's gateway to Southeast Asia; A land-locked neighbour

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Myanmar is called India's gateway to Southeast Asia.
Describe the ancient Uttarapatha route linking India with Central Asia via Afghanistan.
Describe the ancient cultural links and recent cooperation between India and Afghanistan.

topics.title: SAARC, Sri Lanka and the Maldives
topics.ncert_sections: India's Maritime Neighbours; India's nearest maritime neighbour; A nation of islets

concepts.learning_objective: State the purpose and members of SAARC.
Describe the geographical closeness and the cultural ties and difficulties between India and Sri Lanka.
Explain the cultural links between India and the Maldives and the Maldives' climate concerns.

topics.title: Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia
topics.ncert_sections: From Dvaraka to Dvaravati; The Malay Peninsula; The 'Lion City'; The Indonesian archipelago

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret Indian-derived names in Thailand as evidence of cultural exchange.
Compare the historical and present-day links of Malaysia and Singapore with India.
Explain Indonesia's ties with India and their cooperation after the 2004 tsunami.

topics.title: Iran and Oman
topics.ncert_sections: An Ancient Neighbour; The 'Land of Copper'

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the ancient and modern links between India and Iran, including Chabahar Port.
Describe the ancient trade and present defence ties between India and Oman.

topics.title: Harshavardhana, the 'Great King of Kings'
topics.ncert_sections: The 'Great King of Kings'

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Harshavardhana's rule from Kannauj, his patronage of scholars and the limits of his expansion.
Explain why Xuanzang travelled to India and why his travelogue is an important historical source.

topics.title: The Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj
topics.ncert_sections: A Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj; The Palas; The Gurjara-Pratiharas; The Rashtrakutas

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the three powers that fought over Kannauj and explain why no lasting victor emerged.
Describe the Palas' patronage of Buddhist learning, including the university of Vikramashila.
Match the major Gurjara-Pratihara and Rashtrakuta rulers with their achievements.

topics.title: Kashmir
topics.ncert_sections: Kashmir

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Kalhana's method and purpose in writing the Rajatarangini.
Identify important rulers of Kashmir such as Lalitaditya Muktapida and Queen Didda.
Describe Kashmir's role as a centre of Sanskrit learning, Kashmir Shaivism and Buddhist scholarship.

topics.title: The Deccan and the South
topics.ncert_sections: The Deccan and Beyond; The Chalukyas; The Pallavas; Further South

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the rivalry of the Chalukyas and Pallavas and evaluate sources such as the Aihole inscription.
Trace the re-emergence of the Pandyas, Cheras and Cholas in the far south.

topics.title: Polity, Economy and Society
topics.ncert_sections: Other Developments: Polity and administration; Trade, economy and urbanisation; Social life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how kings governed through samantas and directly controlled provinces, districts and villages.
Describe the expansion of land grants, agriculture and maritime trade in this period.
Explain how jatis multiplied and why the varna-jati system remained flexible.

topics.title: Cultural Life and Science
topics.ncert_sections: Cultural life; A galaxy of mathematicians and astronomers

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the coexistence of religious traditions and the spread of the Bhakti tradition.
Identify the contributions of Brahmagupta, Bhaskara I, Virahanka and Mahavira.

topics.title: Foreign Invasions
topics.ncert_sections: Foreign Invasions: The Hunas' challenge; The Arabs arrive on India's shores

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Huna invasions, their defeat and their assimilation into Indian society.
Explain the Arab conquest of Sindh and why Arab gains in India remained limited.
Describe the trade and scientific exchanges between India and the Arab world.

topics.title: The Ghaznavid Invasions
topics.ncert_sections: The Ghaznavid Invasions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Hindu Shahis' control of the Khyber Pass made their resistance to invaders important.
Describe the main events of Mahmud of Ghazni's campaigns in India, including Mathura, Kannauj and Somnath.
Evaluate the evidence historians use to discuss Mahmud's motives for his raids.

topics.title: Scholars of the Age: al-Biruni and Bhaskaracharya
topics.ncert_sections: Al-Biruni; Bhaskaracharya

concepts.learning_objective: Describe al-Biruni's study of Indian knowledge and his remarks on the effects of Mahmud's campaigns.
Identify Bhaskaracharya's major works and explain why they were valued by students.

topics.title: Eastern India and the Kingdoms of the Deccan
topics.ncert_sections: Eastern India; Further South; The Kakatiyas; The Hoysalas

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the Senas and Eastern Gangas, their regions and their cultural contributions.
Describe how the Kakatiyas and Hoysalas rose in the Deccan and what they are remembered for.

topics.title: The Cholas, Masters of the Seas
topics.ncert_sections: The Cholas, masters of the seas

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the conquests and policies of Rajaraja Chola I and the later decline of the Cholas.
Explain the causes and nature of Rajendra Chola I's naval expedition against Srivijaya.

topics.title: Back to the North: the Paramaras and the Ghurids
topics.ncert_sections: Back to the North; The Paramaras; A turning point: the Ghurids in India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the achievements of Bhoja Paramara as a ruler, builder and scholar.
Explain how Muhammad Ghuri's conquest differed from Mahmud's raids and led to lasting rule.
Describe Bakhtiyar Khilji's campaigns in eastern India and their impact on centres of learning.

topics.title: Governance, Trade and Cultural Life
topics.ncert_sections: Governance, Trade and Cultural Life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how kingdoms of this period were administered and what sustained their economy.
Describe the ideas of Ramanujacharya and Basavanna and their impact on society.

topics.title: Taking Stock: Change and Continuity
topics.ncert_sections: Taking Stock

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between the changes and the continuities of the 11th and 12th centuries.
Explain how Angkor Wat shows the influence of Indian traditions in Southeast Asia.
Describe how the Bene Israel came to India and where they settled.
Explain how the Jews of Kochi were welcomed and able to practise their faith.
Interpret Swami Vivekananda's 1893 words about India sheltering the persecuted.
Explain why Syriac Christians left West Asia and settled on the Malabar coast.
Describe how Arab merchants settled on India's west coast as peaceful traders.
Explain why the Parsis left Persia and how they settled at Sanjan in Gujarat.
Compare the similarities and differences between Zoroastrian and Vedic traditions.

topics.title: The Siddis, the Armenians and the Baha'is

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the African origin of the Siddis and the fusion in their culture.
Describe the roles and lasting legacy of Armenians in Indian cities.
Explain why Baha'is came to India and how the faith grew here.

topics.title: The Polish Children and Tibetan Refugees

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the Maharaja of Nawanagar sheltered Polish orphans during the Second World War.
Explain how India sheltered and rehabilitated Tibetan refugees after 1959.
Identify Sowa Rigpa as a Tibetan system of medicine linked with Ayurveda.
Explain how values like vasudhaiva kutumbakam and atithi devo bhava made India a home for many.
Describe how Indians living abroad carry these values of peaceful coexistence.

chapters.title: The State, the Government, and You

topics.title: What is a State?
topics.ncert_sections: What is a State?

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the four features of a state: people, territory, government and sovereignty.
Explain why sovereignty is an essential feature of a state.

topics.title: What is a Government?
topics.ncert_sections: What is a Government?; People, police, and the government

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between the permanent state and the changing government that acts on its behalf.
Describe the role of the police as agents of the state government.

topics.title: Democracy and Republic
topics.ncert_sections: Democracy and Republic; India, a Republic that Protects the Rights of All

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a democracy (rule by the people) from a republic (elected head of state).
Explain how a constitution protects rights against the dominance of the majority.

topics.title: Legislature and Executive
topics.ncert_sections: Legislature: The Lawmaking Body; Executive: The Law-Implementing and Policymaking Body

concepts.learning_objective: State the role of the legislature as the lawmaking body at union and state levels.
Distinguish between the elected political executive and the permanent executive of civil servants.
Describe the key functions of the bureaucracy and its grassroots workers.

topics.title: The Government and You
topics.ncert_sections: The Government and You

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the triple role of the government as protector, provider and regulator.
Identify ways citizens can make the government work, such as grievance portals, RTI, media, NGOs and voting.

topics.title: Judiciary: Guardian of the Constitution
topics.ncert_sections: Judiciary: Guardian of the Constitution

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the functions of an independent judiciary.
Explain the rule of law and why the judiciary is needed to uphold it.

topics.title: Tiers of Government and Decentralisation
topics.ncert_sections: Tiers of Government; What is decentralisation?

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the union, state and local tiers of government and their responsibilities.
Explain what decentralisation means and why it is important in India.

topics.title: Physical infrastructure and why it matters
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Why is physical infrastructure important?

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main forms of physical infrastructure and how they work together.
Explain how physical infrastructure supports people, businesses, trade, emergencies and national security.

topics.title: Roads, highways and bridges
topics.ncert_sections: Transportation Infrastructure (a) Road and highway network

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish local roads, state highways, national highways and expressways and who maintains them.
Explain how bridges such as the Dhola Sadiya Bridge and living root bridges overcome difficult terrain.

topics.title: Railways and metro train systems
topics.ncert_sections: Transportation Infrastructure (b) Indian railway network; (c) Metro train systems

concepts.learning_objective: State why the British introduced railways in India in 1853.
Describe the role of Indian Railways today in moving people and goods, employment and electrification.
Explain how metro trains make city travel faster and cleaner.

topics.title: Air transport, shipping and ports
topics.ncert_sections: Transportation Infrastructure (d) Air transport; (e) Shipping and ports

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the uses of passenger and cargo flights, including during disasters.
Describe the role of ships and ports in carrying heavy goods and in India's trade.

topics.title: Communications infrastructure
topics.ncert_sections: Communications Infrastructure

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the parts of communication infrastructure that carry messages across places.
Explain how communication infrastructure supports education, emergencies, e-commerce and e-governance.
Trace key milestones in communication, including J.C. Bose's work on wireless transmission.

topics.title: Collective responsibility towards infrastructure
topics.ncert_sections: Collective Responsibility Towards Infrastructure; Infrastructure in the Arthashastra

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why caring for public infrastructure is the shared duty of citizens and government.
Explain how infrastructure can be made sustainable and suitable for children, the elderly and disabled persons.
Describe how Kautilya's Arthashastra regulated roads and protected public works.

chapters.title: Banks and the Magic of Finance

topics.title: Financial infrastructure and what banks do
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; What are banks and what do they do?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what financial infrastructure is and how it supports physical infrastructure.
Describe how a bank links savers who deposit money with borrowers who need loans.

topics.title: Holding deposits: types of bank accounts and the passbook
topics.ncert_sections: Hold deposits; Types of bank accounts (Fig. 8.4); Passbook

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
Interpret debit and credit entries recorded in a bank passbook.

topics.title: Interest and the magic of compounding
topics.ncert_sections: Interest on deposits; The Magic of Compounding - the story of a King and a Sage

concepts.learning_objective: Define interest as the cost of borrowing or the gain from lending money.
Calculate how a deposit grows when interest is earned on earlier interest.
Use the king and sage chessboard story to explain exponential growth.

topics.title: Loans, how banks earn, and the Jan Dhan Yojana
topics.ncert_sections: Offer loans or credit; Don't miss out; Jan Dhan Yojana

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the purposes for which people and businesses take bank loans.
Explain how the gap between deposit and loan interest rates gives banks income.
Describe how the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana widened access to banking.

topics.title: Other financial institutions and the Reserve Bank of India
topics.ncert_sections: Other Financial Institutions; Reserve Bank of India - Banker to Banks; Temples as lenders

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the financial roles of post offices, NABARD and the Industrial Finance Corporation of India.
State the functions of the RBI as India's central bank and banker to banks.
Compare the lending role of temples in ancient India with modern banks.

topics.title: Payment modes and systems
topics.ncert_sections: Payment Modes and Systems; Cheque; Debit cards and POS; Internet banking; Mobile payments; UPI

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how cash is withdrawn using a withdrawal slip or a debit card at an ATM.
Compare cheques with electronic payment methods such as POS machines and internet banking.
Explain the steps of a UPI transaction and why UPI became popular.

topics.title: Stock market
topics.ncert_sections: Stock Market

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what a share is and why companies issue shares on a stock exchange.
Analyse the factors that cause share prices to rise and fall, leading to booms and crashes.

topics.title: Financial frauds and the role of financial infrastructure
topics.ncert_sections: Financial frauds and how to prevent them; Before we move on

concepts.learning_objective: Apply safety practices to avoid and report digital payment frauds.
Evaluate how financial infrastructure contributes to a nation's progress.
